## Objective
- Build a complete playable 3D zombie survival FPS in the empty repo, featuring as many weapons as possible, with polished visuals, HUD, menu, armory, waves, mobile controls, and verification screenshots.

## Requirements
- User request (Portuguese): “Crie um jogo de zumbi com todas as armas existentes que vc puder em 3D”.
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save verification screenshots as small JPEGs, viewport max 1280px wide; read only latest screenshot.
- Use full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JS game served by existing `start.sh` runtime on port 3002; no framework or build step.
- Vendored Three.js r0.160.0 locally under `vendor/three/`.
- 26 procedurally modeled weapons across 8 categories, all unlocked from the start.
- Procedural textures, models, particle effects, and WebAudio synthesis; no external runtime assets.
- Portuguese UI, title “ZONA MORTA — ÚLTIMA RESISTÊNCIA”.
- Main menu Play button has `aria-label="Play"` so automated capture can start gameplay.
- Wave-based survival with 5 zombie classes plus boss every 5 waves.
- Touch controls and responsive layout for phones/tablets.
- Player can choose weapons via mouse wheel, quick categories (1–8), or armory (Tab).

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected repo and environment; confirmed empty project with static `index.html` support.
- Vendored Three.js core and postprocessing addons.
- Downloaded and vendored local WOFF2 fonts.
- Created `index.html` with menu, HUD, armory, pause, game-over, scope, wave banner, intermission, touch controls, loader.
- Created `styles.css` with full industrial horror UI, responsive/mobile styles, HUD layout, overlays.
- Created `src/weapons.js` with 26 weapon definitions, procedural 3D models, armory metadata, stats.
- Created `src/textures.js` with procedural asphalt, concrete, metal, chainlink, blood, moon, warning, skyline, etc.
- Created `src/world.js` with arena, containers, bus, watchtower, fences, fires, floodlights, props, lighting, collision, raycasts, spawn points.
- Created `src/effects.js` with particle pools, tracers, impact/blood decals, gibs, explosions, lightning, fire/frost.
- Created `src/audio.js` with synthesized guns, reload, hits, zombie groans, explosions, waves, ambience.
- Created `src/zombies.js` with procedural zombie models, animations, AI, status effects, projectile acid, boss support.
- Created `src/thumbnails.js` to render real weapon thumbnails from 3D models.
- Created `src/main.js` with renderer/scene setup, menu, game lifecycle, HUD, input, touch, waves, shooting, projectiles, pickups, radar, explosions, armory, pause, death, and main loop.

### Active
- Code integration is largely written but has not yet been syntax-checked or run.
- Needs review/fixes in `src/main.js` and `src/zombies.js`, especially newly appended methods.
- Needs full browser verification and screenshots.
- Needs final brief note on assumptions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check` or an ES module syntax check for all `src/*.js`; fix errors.
2. Start the game via existing `start.sh` in a persistent session and verify HTTP on port 3002.
3. Use `playwright-cli` to open `http://localhost:3002`, auto-click Play, and capture a JPEG screenshot ≤1280px.
4. Inspect latest screenshot for blank canvas, loader, menu, broken HUD, missing weapons, or page errors; fix iteratively.
5. Verify gameplay essentials manually: movement, firing, reload, weapon switching, armory, waves, zombies, damage, death/retry, touch layout.
6. Check page console for shader/WebGL/JS errors, especially particle shader attributes and `ZombieManager.onKill`.
7. Capture final desktop screenshot and possibly mobile screenshot.
8. Finish with concise Portuguese/English summary of what was built and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: full UI structure and import map.
- `styles.css`: all menu/HUD/responsive styling.
- `src/main.js`: central game logic; likely where errors remain.
- `src/weapons.js`: 26 weapon definitions and procedural models.
- `src/world.js`: arena, environment, collision, raycasts.
- `src/zombies.js`: zombie models/AI/manager.
- `src/effects.js`: particle and combat effects.
- `src/audio.js`: synthesized audio.
- `src/textures.js`: procedural canvas textures.
- `src/thumbnails.js`: armory/menu weapon thumbnail renderer.
- `vendor/three/three.module.js`: vendored Three.js.
- `vendor/three/addons/`: vendored postprocessing/shaders.
- `assets/fonts/`: vendored font files.
- `start.sh`: runtime static server entry point.
- `capture.sh`: runtime screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- Repo had no `package.json`; adding one may break static serving, so do not add a framework/package project unless deliberately changing `start.sh`.
- Existing `start.sh` calls `$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs`, which supports plain static `index.html`.
- Automated capture’s start selector recognizes buttons with exact visible text “Play/Start” or `aria-label="Play"`; `#playBtn` has `aria-label="Play"` and visible text “JOGAR”.
- `CAPTURE_AUTO_START` defaults true; screenshot is taken ~1s after clicking Play, so wave 1 spawns immediately and the HUD must be ready quickly.
- Need to confirm `ZombieManager` constructor sets `this.onKill`; it was patched after initial file creation.
- `src/main.js` references module-level `rand(a,b)` declared after the class, which is valid; verify no use before initialization at constructor time.
- Potential issue: `#intermission` CSS likely needs `pointer-events: none` so it does not block aiming/firing.
- Potential issue: particle shader in `src/effects.js` declares `attribute vec3 color;` with `vertexColors: true`; verify no duplicate/compilation conflict.
- Potential issue: `src/main.js` `cacheDom` converts `damage-vignette` to `damageVignette`; it later overwrites via explicit query, so verify all refs resolve.
- Potential issue: in `updateWeaponRig`, `this.weaponRig.visible = !scoped` means scoped weapons hide correctly but branch sets visible again after early return; verify.
- Potential issue: automatic fire for semi-auto/pump logic may fire continuously due `this.firing` handling; test.
- Potential issue: `this.waveStats` and `this.spawnQueue` may be accessed before initialization in `startWave`/HUD; verify.
- User wants all existing weapons; current arsenal: M1911, Desert Eagle, Ray Gun, MP5, UMP-45, P90, AK-47, M4A1, SCAR-H, Remington 870, SPAS-12, AA-12, AWP, Barrett M82, M249 SAW, M134 Minigun, RPG-7, M32 MGL, Flamethrower, Crossbow, Nailgun, Tesla Cannon, Cryo Ray, Machete, Katana, Chainsaw.
- No commits have been made during this work.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete playable 3D zombie survival FPS in the empty repo, with as many weapons as possible, polished visuals, HUD, menu, armory, waves, mobile controls, and verification screenshots.

## Requirements
- User request (Portuguese): “Crie um jogo de zumbi com todas as armas existentes que vc puder em 3D”.
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save verification screenshots as small JPEGs, viewport max 1280px wide; read only latest screenshot.
- Use full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JS game served by existing `start.sh`; no framework or build step.
- Vendored Three.js r0.160.0 locally under `vendor/three/`.
- 26 procedurally modeled weapons across 8 categories, all unlocked from the start.
- Procedural textures, models, particle effects, and WebAudio synthesis; no external runtime assets.
- Portuguese UI, title “ZONA MORTA — ÚLTIMA RESISTÊNCIA”.
- Main menu Play button has `aria-label="Play"` / `id="playBtn"` for automated capture.
- Wave-based survival with 5 zombie classes plus boss every 5 waves.
- Touch controls and responsive layout for phones/tablets.
- Player can choose weapons via mouse wheel, quick categories (1–8), or armory (Tab).
- Desktop server actually binds port **3000**, not 3002.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected repo/environment; confirmed empty static project.
- Vendored Three.js core/addons and local WOFF2 fonts.
- Built `index.html`, `styles.css`, all `src/*.js` modules, 26 weapon models, world, effects, audio, zombies, thumbnails, main loop.
- All modules pass `node --check`; browser loads with zero console errors.
- Menu screenshot verified as visually strong; gameplay, AI, damage, wave HUD, game-over flow all verified live.
- Fixed shader `attribute vec3 color` redefinition; fixed crossbow category typo `SPECIAL` → `ESPECIAL`; fixed undefined `this.crosshair`/`this.scopeOverlay`; made intermission `pointer-events:none`; added favicon.
- Added layer-1 dedicated viewmodel lighting; pulled/scaled weapon rig; reduced flashlight blowout; darkened zombie palettes; reduced eye size/intensity and bloom.
- Confirmed death/game-over screen renders correctly; stats show zero when idle.

### Active
- Fine-tuning weapon viewmodel framing/scale and overall lighting; newest tuning edits just applied but not yet re-verified.
- Need to verify shooting, reload, weapon switching, armory, grenades, explosions, wave clear/intermission, boss, retry, mobile layout.
- Need to improve thumbnail camera/lighting (AK floating image currently reads blocky and lacks hero composition).
- Need final clean screenshots after tuning.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload and start fresh game; capture JPEG and inspect new weapon rig (`scale .66`, base `.28,-.27,-.9`, yaw `-.16`) and lighting changes.
2. Fix zombie overexposure/creepy-cartoon look further if needed (skin, eye glow, flashlight falloff).
3. Improve `src/thumbnails.js` camera to flatter, brighter 3/4 side profile (longer lens, e.g. fov ~22, distance ~7.6, bright key/rim).
4. Test combat: fire, reload (`R`), weapon cycle, armory (`Tab`), grenade (`G`), hitmarkers, kills/score.
5. Test wave clear/intermission, boss wave, pause/resume, restart, death/retry.
6. Verify mobile/touch viewport screenshot and responsive HUD.
7. Capture final desktop gameplay/menu JPEGs ≤1280px; check console errors.
8. Finish with concise summary in Portuguese/English plus key assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: central game logic, viewmodel rig, input, waves, HUD, armory, projectiles; most tuning happens here.
- `src/zombies.js`: zombie models/AI/manager, palettes/eyes, boss and explosions.
- `src/weapons.js`: 26 weapon definitions and procedural models.
- `src/thumbnails.js`: menu/armory weapon thumbnail renderer; needs camera/lighting polish.
- `src/world.js`: arena, lighting, collision, raycasts, spawn points.
- `src/effects.js`: particle pools, tracers, impacts, explosions.
- `src/audio.js`: synthesized gun/zombie/explosion audio.
- `src/textures.js`: procedural textures.
- `index.html`: UI structure, import map, favicon.
- `styles.css`: menu/HUD/armory/responsive styling.
- `vendor/three/`: vendored Three.js runtime and postprocessing addons.
- `assets/fonts/`: vendored WOFF2 fonts.
- `start.sh`: runtime entry point; serves on port 3000.
- `screenshots/`: latest checks (`menu2.jpg`, `game4.jpg`, `rig3.jpg`, `rig4.jpg` death screen).
- `capture.sh`: runtime screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- Playwright server: `http://localhost:3000` is running via background `./start.sh`; port 3002 is not used.
- Chromium was installed via `playwright-cli install-browser chrome-for-testing`; session name `zm`.
- Playwright viewport currently 1280×800.
- Automated capture clicks `aria-label="Play"`; `CAPTURE_AUTO_START` defaults true, screenshot ~1s after click, so HUD must be ready immediately.
- Game auto-starts wave 1 with 5 zombies; idling ~2 minutes lets zombies kill the player (game-over verified).
- Weapon rig uses camera layers: world on layer 0, viewmodel meshes on layer 1, dedicated `gunKey`/`gunFill`/`gunAmbient` lights on layer 1; main flashlight is layer 0.
- `window.__ZONA_MORTA__` exposes the Game instance for live Playwright tuning.
- No commits made; all work uncommitted in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`.

The landscape mobile menu looks good. But some text is clipped at the bottom (stats row partially cut, version). It fits 915x412 but height is tight. The Play button visible, Arsenal. Good enough. Notice the hero weapon AK is now displayed as a side profile with a "floating" look; the stock is pink/salmon due to thumbnail material and key light. Hmm, in the menu the wood looks salmon/pink rather than wood brown. That's because we raised lightness by 1.55 and the red rim light. In game the wood is orange-brown. In the menu, the AK stock/handguard is salmon pink, which looks odd. It's a bit garish.

We should fix thumbnail lighting/material so wood stays brown, not pink. The lightness lift affects saturated wood colors: 0x6b3c22 HSL hue ~22°, sat .52, lightness .28 → max(.16, .43) = .43, so it becomes 0xb06a3d-ish (lighter orange). Combined with red rim → salmon. Could clamp the lightness lift for already-bright colors: `Math.max(.16, Math.min(.34, hsl.l * 1.55))`. That would keep wood at .34 (light brown) and dark metal at .16. Good. Also reduce red rim intensity or make it more subtle. The red rim helps atmosphere; keep 12.

Let's adjust lightness clamp to .32 and saturation * .85. Wood becomes less pastel. Also maybe increase key warmth.

Then mobile landscape gameplay screenshot.
Image read successfully

Mobile landscape gameplay looks quite good. The touch controls are visible: joystick bottom-left, fire button bottom-right, buttons REC, MIRA, SALTO, ARMA, and quick weapon buttons at the bottom center. But there are some issues:

1. The "FUZIL DE..." text in the bottom-right above the weapon quick buttons is overlapping the touch controls. The weapon slot label "07 / 26" is clipped, and the ammo count 30/240 is at the very bottom behind the fire button? Actually the ammo readout (30 / 240) is behind/under the fire button on the right, partially cut off (I see "30" at x~886 y=320 in the fire button area, and "240" at bottom right). This is a HUD layout bug on mobile landscape: the weapon/ammo readout collides with the fire controls.

2. The health/armor bottom-left overlaps the joystick? The joystick is above the health bar; looks okay. But "INTEGRIDADE" label near the joystick and health 100 at bottom, plus "PLACAS SD" and armor bar are cut off at the bottom edge? The screenshot height 412; bottom UI is at y=390-412, maybe partially clipped. "PLACAS SD" text at y=382 and armor bar at 397, visible. OK.

3. The wave header at top: "ONDA 01" centered, "5 HOSTIS" right. Score 0 top right. Good.

4. The scene lighting on mobile is very warm/orange (flashlight color 0xffe1b0 + fog), almost sepia. The desktop was cooler. This is because mobile uses a different flashlight intensity? Actually the touch flashlight is 4 vs desktop 5 and same color; the scene looks orange due to the floodlight cones maybe. It's okay, but the road is very brown. Hmm.

5. The gun viewmodel on mobile: we see the AK from the right side, looks decent, positioned center-right. But the mobile canvas is wider; gun at bottom center. Fine.

6. The touch quick weapon buttons at bottom center are tiny (PSR SMG RIF SNP LMG ESP MEL) and overlapping the "ARMA ATIVA 07 / 26" text. The quick buttons are placed along the bottom center, partially behind the "FUZIL DE ASSALTO" label. Actually the label "ARMA ATIVA 07 / 26" is above the buttons at y=365, and "FUZIL DE..." at 355 on the right, cut by the fire controls. It's acceptable but cramped.

Main fix: hide or reposition the weapon block (ammo readout, weapon name/category) on mobile so it doesn't collide with touch controls. Perhaps on mobile, move the ammo readout to top-right under score, or bottom-right above the fire button but with smaller size. And move/hide the "weapon slot" text.

sed -n '670,730p' styles.css
